stageMeta.title: Multi-Agent
headerComment: # Stage 08 — Multi-Agent
# L8 = L7 + Delegation.  Every plugin from Stage 06 is still here — sandbox,
# approval, FS, shell, search, persistence, resume — plus the two capability
# closures that grew in between:
#   L7 — Stateful Task Agent:
#     dsh-tool-todo        model-facing todo_write (whole-list replacement)
#     dsh-user-questions   user-questions seam (ctx.userQuestions) backing the
#                          exit_plan_mode review
#     dsh-plan-mode        logged plan/mode state + exit_plan_mode review
#     dsh-goal             event-sourced same-session goal domain (ctx.goals)
#     dsh-tool-goal        model-facing get/create/update_goal tools
#     dsh-storage          storage hub (ctx.storage) — backend registry
#     dsh-storage-sqlite   SQLite backend, registers as backend "sqlite"
#     dsh-storage-domain   domain data form, provides ctx.storageDomain
#     dsh-workspace        workspace entity registry (ctx.workspaceRegistry)
#   L8 — Multi-Agent:
#     dsh-subagent                  subagent registry: ctx.subagents, the
#                                   process-singleton seam ("Agent as a provider")
#     dsh-subagent-spawn-in-process provider "spawn": fresh child, no history
#     dsh-subagent-fork-in-process  provider "fork":  child seeded with the
#                                   parent's completed turns
#     dsh-tool-subagent             model-facing delegation tool; mounted twice
#                                   (subagent → spawn, subagent_fork → fork)
#     dsh-jobs                      ABSTRACT background-job registry seam —
#                                   its constructor throws by design when
#                                   mounted directly, so it is listed disabled
#     dsh-jobs-local                process-local ctx.jobs implementation
#     dsh-tool-jobs                 model-facing job control (job_list /
#                                   job_output / job_kill + completion notices)
# Architecture concept: Agent as a provider.  The subagent seam is a registry
# of named providers; spawn/fork decide HOW the child runs, the delegation
# tool decides THAT the model can ask for one.  Changing the provider changes
# transport without changing the execution contract.  Both in-process
# providers share @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-in-process-driver — a plain
# library (no plugin exports), so there is nothing to mount for it.
# Observable behavior (with --trace): a subagent delegation appears as
# tool/call (subagent) → the child's own session events (turn/start …) →
# tool/result carrying only the child's final message back to the parent.
# The child's intermediate steps never enter the parent's history.
# The persona is frozen (byte-for-byte identical to L4/L5/L6) so the
# progression remains a true single-variable experiment.
# Second L8 closure — subagent control plane:
#   dsh-tool-subagent-control            global send_message / interrupt_agent
#   dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents  schema registers now, calls go live
#                                          when session-projection arrives (L10)
#   dsh-tool-subagent-report             child-scoped `report` over continuations
# The control plane is wired but inert until a subagent instance sets
# backgroundMode: continuable — one-shot children accept no follow-ups.
stageMeta.driverQuestion: Use the subagent tool to delegate an investigation: have a subagent read src/calculator.js, find the bug in it, and report back. Then summarize what the subagent found.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Required, non-empty (unknown keys fail at load): the guidance section
    # rendered at prompt order 50 while plan mode is active.
    section: |
      You are in plan mode. Explore and design before presenting the complete
      plan through exit_plan_mode.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-goal
entry.configYaml:
config:
    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 256   # the schema default, written out for visibility

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal
comments: # blockedAfterConsecutiveRounds defaults to 3; no override needed here.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-sqlite
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Backend registers on the hub under the fixed name "sqlite".  path is
    # required (':memory:' allowed); a file keeps workspace records durable
    # next to the session logs inside the disposable run root.
    path: ./storage/domain.db
    # journalMode defaults to 'wal'.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent
comments: # The seam itself: registers ctx.subagents, the process-singleton registry
# of named subagent providers, plus the delegation-depth vocabulary and the
# subagent/start ↔ subagent/end lifecycle events.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-spawn-in-process
comments: # Provider "spawn" (default providerName): fresh child Agent in this
# process — own session, inherits cwd/model, sees NO parent history.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-fork-in-process
comments: # Provider "fork" (default providerName): same in-process run mechanics as
# spawn, but the child's session is seeded with the parent's completed
# turns (the contiguous prefix ending at the last turn/end).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # First instance → the `subagent` tool over the spawn provider.
    # Defaults kept: backgroundMode one-shot (foreground unless the model
    # passes run_in_background), maxDepth 3, background calls enabled.
    # The tool registers only while its provider exists — with spawn mounted
    # above, the `subagent` schema appears in the parent's tool registry.
    provider: spawn

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # Second instance → the `subagent_fork` tool over the fork provider.
    # One plugin instance binds exactly one provider to one tool name, so
    # exposing both transports requires two distinctly named instances.
    provider: fork
    toolName: subagent_fork

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs
comments: # dsh-jobs is the ABSTRACT job-registry contract: mounting it directly
# throws by design ("load an implementation such as dsh-jobs-local
# instead").  It is listed here, disabled, so the closure stays visible
# in inspect/diff; the concrete registry below provides ctx.jobs.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs-local
comments: # Process-local JobRegistry (default maxConcurrentJobsPerOwner: 10).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs
comments: # Model-facing job control: job_list / job_output / job_kill plus
# completion notices; also attaches the per-owner job controller that
# ctx.jobs.start() requires, which is what makes one-shot BACKGROUND
# subagent delegation (run_in_background: true) collectable.
# Config defaults kept: waitTimeoutMs 30s, maxWaitTimeoutMs 600s,
# completionDelivery 'wakeup', maxConsecutiveWakes 3.
